blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Navigation by Numbers
blocks.content: A bearing is a way to describe direction using a single number measured in degrees. Sailors, pilots, and hikers all use bearings to navigate. Instead of saying 'go slightly east of north', you say 'go on a bearing of 040 degrees'. It's precise, universal, and eliminates all confusion about direction.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Three Golden Laws
blocks.content:
Bearings ALWAYS follow three strict rules:

• **Rule 1:** Always measure from NORTH (the 12 o'clock position).
• **Rule 2:** Always measure CLOCKWISE.
• **Rule 3:** Always write as a THREE-figure number (so 40 degrees becomes 040 degrees, and 5 degrees becomes 005 degrees).

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Finding a Bearing
blocks.content:
To find the bearing of point B from point A:

1. Stand at point A and draw a line pointing directly NORTH (straight up).
2. Draw a line from A to B.
3. Measure the angle CLOCKWISE from the North line to the line AB.
4. Write the answer as three digits.

To find the RETURN bearing (B back to A), add or subtract 180 degrees.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Return Bearings
blocks.content:
The bearing of B from A is 130 degrees. Find the bearing of A from B.

**Step 1:** The original bearing is 130.
**Step 2:** Since 130 < 180, we ADD 180.
**Step 3:** 130 + 180 = 310.

**Final Answer: The bearing of A from B is 310 degrees.**
(If the result were > 360, you'd subtract 360.)

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: Two deadly mistakes: (1) Measuring ANTICLOCKWISE instead of clockwise. Bearings are ALWAYS clockwise from North. (2) Writing a two-digit answer like '40' instead of '040'. Bearings must ALWAYS be three digits. An examiner will mark you wrong for writing 40 instead of 040, even though mathematically they're the same number!
